oewn-02714280-v.learner: to use up a stretch of time in a particular way
examples: The rest of the evening was spent in conjecturing how soon he would return Mr. Bennet's visit.
The town where they were now to spend a few days was probably as great an object of her curiosity.
She spends far too much on new gowns and ribbons.
They spent thirty pounds on the horse.

oewn-02272374-v.learner: to use something up until none of it is left
examples: He spends his whole allowance the day he receives it.

oewn-14460341-n.learner: the state of being treated with great respect
examples: I thank you again and again for the honour you have done me in your proposals.
I had not at that time the honour of knowing any lady in the assembly beyond my own party.

oewn-04876319-n.learner: the quality of acting rightly and having a good name
examples: she was proud of him, proud that in a cause of compassion and honour he had been able to get the better of himself
But upon my honour I do not.

oewn-06709228-n.learner: a thing you can hold or see that is given to show approval or to mark someone out
examples: The medal was the greatest honour he had ever received.

oewn-02458316-v.learner: to keep something from happening or coming about, or to make it impossible
examples: she could not prevent its frequently recurring
Regard for my sister's credit and feelings prevented any public exposure.

oewn-02455370-v.learner: to stop a person or thing from doing something, or from being in a certain state
examples: Mrs. Bennet was prevented replying by the entrance of the footman with a note for Miss Bennet.
if he had been prevented going, the wedding need not be put off

oewn-13948785-n.learner: the conditions or place you find yourself in
examples: that being the case, I cannot consider your situation with much compassion
the wife of Mr. Darcy must have such extraordinary sources of happiness necessarily attached to her situation

oewn-08640525-n.learner: where a thing stands, seen against what is around it
examples: He did look at it, and into it, for half an hour; was pleased with the situation and the principal rooms.

oewn-00587299-n.learner: a job that someone holds in a company or other organization
examples: as to his future situation, he could conjecture very little about it
She took a situation as a governess in a large household.

oewn-01733798-s.learner: belonging to a time before now
examples: she set off again in quest of her former acquaintance
how gradually all her former prejudices had been removed

oewn-01051000-a.learner: pointing to the first of two people or things just named, or to the earlier one or ones of several
examples: When Jane and Elizabeth were alone, the former, who had been cautious in her praise of Mr. Bingley, expressed how much she admired him.
she was seated between Charlotte and Miss de Bourgh--the former of whom was engaged in listening to Lady Catherine

oewn-01734051-s.learner: being what someone was until very recently
examples: The former president spoke at the dinner.

oewn-09869006-n.learner: a person who is loved; a name you call someone you are fond of
examples: Write to me very often, my dear.

connotation.why: an affectionate name rather than a plain word for a person

oewn-10263569-n.learner: a sweet, gentle person who means no harm, above all a child
examples: She is such a dear, and never has a hard word for anyone.

connotation.why: sets the person down as sweet and harmless

oewn-00611721-v.learner: to put something out of your mind and stop keeping it in memory
examples: I cannot forget the follies and vices of others so soon as I ought
causes which I had myself endeavoured to forget, because they were not immediately before me

oewn-00616520-v.learner: to fail to do something because you did not remember to do it
examples: They had forgotten to leave any message.

oewn-00610654-v.learner: to be unable to bring something back to mind
examples: I have forgotten his name, though I met him only last week.

oewn-09937706-n.learner: someone's son or daughter, at any age
examples: Mr. Bennet, how can you abuse your own children in such a way?
I and my children must have had all his money

oewn-09937051-n.learner: a young person, boy or girl
examples: A crowd of children were playing in the lane.

oewn-09938012-n.learner: a grown person who behaves as a child does
examples: In money matters he was a child to the end of his life.

connotation.why: marks a grown person as not grown up

oewn-02873453-n.learner: an object made of many pages fastened together
examples: The book was heavy, and its pages were coming loose from the binding.

oewn-06422547-n.learner: a piece of writing that has been printed on pages and put out for people to read
examples: I have often observed how little young ladies are interested by books of a serious stamp.
my father should have left so small a collection of books

oewn-06406508-n.learner: one of the large parts a long written work is divided into
examples: The storm is described in the second book of the poem.

oewn-01414308-a.learner: having a good chance of being true or of happening
examples: I wonder whether he is likely to be in this country much longer.
She was convinced that she could have been happy with him, when it was no longer likely they should meet.
That is not a very likely excuse.

oewn-01890275-s.learner: expected to become or be something
examples: He is the likely winner of the prize.
